statement: No agreement between the two leading compute jurisdictions sets verifiable limits on training compute or capabilities (official readouts, treaty texts; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Condition held throughout 2024. 2024 was the high point of bilateral AI engagement so far: the first intergovernmental AI dialogue (Geneva, May), two UN General Assembly AI resolutions each backed by both blocs (March, July), and a leaders' affirmation (Lima, Nov) that humans, not AI, should control nuclear-use decisions. None of these set limits on training compute or capabilities, and none had verification. Multilateral safety commitments (Bloc H, May) were voluntary and company-level; a regional AI treaty (Sept) was signed by Bloc A but not Bloc B and contains no compute limits.

items.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted by consensus a Bloc A-led, non-binding resolution on 'safe, secure and trustworthy' AI for sustainable development, co-sponsored by Bloc B. No compute or capability limits; no verification.
items.detail: UNGA resolution A/RES/78/265, adopted 2024-03-21 (Bloc A-led, >120 co-sponsors including Bloc B). Not verified via web_extract this run.

items.summary: The two leading compute jurisdictions held their first intergovernmental dialogue on AI risk and safety; both readouts describe an exchange of views only. Bloc A raised misuse concerns; Bloc B protested Bloc A's AI-related restrictions. No agreement, no follow-on limits.
items.detail: Bloc A-Bloc B talks on AI risk and safety, Geneva, 2024-05-14. NSC statement (Bloc A Mission Geneva, 2024-05-15) and gov.cn/CGTN readout (2024-05-16), verified via search snippets.

items.summary: At a multilateral AI summit, 16 developers including a Bloc B firm signed voluntary frontier-safety commitments (publish risk thresholds, possibly not deploy beyond them). Company-level and self-defined; not an intergovernmental limit.
items.detail: AI Bloc H Summit, 2024-05-21/22: 'Frontier AI Safety Commitments' (Bloc G DSIT), signatories incl. Zhipu AI. Not verified via web_extract this run.

items.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted by consensus a Bloc B-led resolution on international cooperation for AI capacity-building, supported by Bloc A. Development-focused; no limits.
items.detail: UNGA resolution A/RES/78/311 'Enhancing international cooperation on capacity-building of artificial intelligence', adopted 2024-07-01. Not verified via web_extract this run.

items.summary: The first binding international AI treaty (human rights, democracy, rule of law) opened for signature and was signed by Bloc A and others, but not Bloc B; it regulates use-risk management and contains no compute or capability limits.
items.detail: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS No. 225), opened for signature in Vilnius 2024-09-05; signed by Bloc A, Bloc G, Bloc C, others. Not verified via web_extract this run.

items.summary: Leaders of the two blocs affirmed the need to maintain human control over decisions to use nuclear weapons and to develop military AI 'prudently' - the first bilateral AI-related commitment, but a political statement with no capability limits or verification.
items.detail: White House readout of the Biden-Xi meeting, Lima, 2024-11-16 (Bloc A Embassy Lima copy, verified via snippet); Reuters 2024-11-16.
